lessons.title: Lesson 102: Quoted Abbreviations
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 102 focus. Use the official Unit 5 lesson for the full explanation and additional examples.

cards.translation: He says that he doesn’t want to go to the night market
cards.explanation: Quoted abbreviations contract longer reported-speech forms such as ~다고 해요, ~(이)라고 해요, ~자고 해요 and ~냐고 해요 into short conversational endings. Use these forms when relaying another person’s statement, question, suggestion or command in casual spoken Korean. They are common in speech but are not automatically appropriate in formal writing. Choose the contraction that matches the quote: ~다고 해요 → ~대요, ~(이)라고 해요 → ~(이)래요, ~자고 해요 → ~재요, and ~냐고 해요 → ~냬요. Keep the tense and honorific details from the original quoted clause.

cards.translation: Of course, during class we learned about that subject, but it was very short and I only studied before the night of the exam so I forgot everything immediately
cards.explanation: The topic particle ~는/은 has additional uses in more complicated sentences beyond its basic topic and contrast roles. Use it to mark a topic, contrast alternatives or frame a clause in the advanced contexts presented by HTSK. Attach 은 after a consonant and 는 after a vowel; choose the particle according to the noun or clause role and the contrast intended.

cards.translation: Exercise vitalizes blood flow

lessons.title: Various uses of ~든지
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 106 focus. Use the official Unit 5 lesson for the full explanation and additional examples.

cards.prompt: 네가 내일 무엇을 ___ 간에 밖에 나가야 돼
cards.translation: It doesn’t matter what you do tomorrow, but you have to go outside
cards.explanation: ~든지 has a broad meaning across several constructions, including whichever, whether or not and either option. Use it when the choice is open, when alternatives do not matter or when emphasizing that any option is acceptable. Attach ~든지 to the appropriate verb, adjective or noun form and repeat it in paired alternatives when required; include 말다 in the whether-or-not pattern.

cards.prompt: 제가 운전을 처음 배웠을 때 초보 운전자 스티커를 붙이고 ___어요
cards.translation: When I first learned how to drive, I drove around with a beginner-driver sticker (on my car) (but now I don’t)
cards.explanation: An extra past ~었 in forms such as 했었다 marks an earlier or formerly true past state and can distinguish it from a later past reference. Use it when looking back on something that had been true or regularly happened before another past point, or is no longer true. Add the extra past marker before the ending: 하 + 였 + 었다 contracts to 했었다, with the regular past and speech-level changes shown by HTSK.

lessons.title: Inference with ~나 보다
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 109 focus. Use the official Unit 5 lesson for the full explanation and additional examples.

cards.translation: I guess this is the resting room
cards.explanation: ~는가 보다, ~나 보다 and ~나 봐 express an inference or conclusion based on evidence: it seems or I guess. Use them when the speaker infers a situation rather than directly witnessing or asserting it as fact. Use the appropriate present, past or future form before 보다; spoken forms such as ~나 봐 follow the contractions and politeness patterns in HTSK.

lessons.title: There is no way / cannot help it
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 110 focus. Use the official Unit 5 lesson for the full explanation and additional examples.

cards.translation: There is no evidence, so there is nothing we can do
cards.explanation: 어쩔 수 없다 means there is no way, nothing can be done or one cannot help it. Use it when circumstances leave no alternative or when an unavoidable result is being accepted. Use the fixed expression 어쩔 수 없다, optionally after a clause explaining the situation; conjugate 없다 for tense and politeness.

lessons.title: At least / even if it is just with ~(이)라도
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 111 focus. Use the official Unit 5 lesson for the full explanation and additional examples.

cards.translation: Now that it is raining, do you want to go to the movies or something? (I’d rather go somewhere else, but it’s raining so what else can we do? How about going to the movies?)
cards.explanation: ~(이)라도 means at least, even if it is just or even one among alternatives. Use it when accepting a less ideal option or choosing a minimum substitute. Attach ~이라도 after a consonant noun and ~라도 after a vowel noun; place it after the noun being offered or selected.

lessons.title: The noun 편 for tendency and preference
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 112 focus. Use the official Unit 5 lesson for the full explanation and additional examples.

cards.translation: That person has a fair amount of money
cards.explanation: 편 is a noun meaning side or tendency and ~는 편이다 describes a tendency, degree or preference. Use it to make a softened generalization such as tending to, being relatively or usually being that way. Use N인 편이다, V-는 편이다 or the appropriate adjective and past forms before 편이다; conjugate 이다 normally.

lessons.title: ~는 길 for the act of doing
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 113 focus. Use the official Unit 5 lesson for the full explanation and additional examples.

cards.translation: The reverend said he is on the way to the church now
cards.explanation: ~는 길 treats 길 as a noun in the expression the way or act of doing something, and can also mean on the way. Use it when describing an action in progress or something done while going somewhere. Put the present modifier ~는 before 길, then add particles such as 에 or 로 and the predicate that HTSK demonstrates.

cards.prompt: 색연필을 사러 ___인데 혹시 필요한 것이 있어요?

Put the present modifier ~는 before 길, then add particles such as 에 or 로 and the predicate that HTSK demonstrates.

lessons.title: While doing something / on the way with ~는 김에
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 114 focus. Use the official Unit 5 lesson for the full explanation and additional examples.

cards.prompt: 병원에 ___ 혈액 검사를 했는데 의사 선생님이 당이 검출됐다고 했어요
cards.translation: While at the hospital I got my blood checked out, and the doctor said sugars were detected
cards.explanation: ~는 김에 means while doing something, taking the opportunity or on the way. Use it when a second action is added because the first action already provides a convenient occasion. Attach the present modifier ~는 to the verb before 김에; the second clause states the extra action.

lessons.title: Regret with ~ㄹ/을걸 그랬다
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 115 focus. Use the official Unit 5 lesson for the full explanation and additional examples.

cards.prompt: 국에 김이 많이 안 나서 안 뜨거울 줄 알았는데 그래도 국자를 ___
cards.translation: There wasn’t a lot of steam coming out of the soup, so I thought it wouldn’t be hot, but either way I should have used a ladle
cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을걸 그랬다 expresses regret about a past choice: I should have or I wish I had. Use it when looking back and wishing the action had been done differently. Attach ~ㄹ걸 그랬다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을걸 그랬다 after another consonant; use the negative form when regretting an action not done.

cards.explanation: ~ㄹ/을걸 그랬다 expresses regret about a past choice: I should have or I wish I had. Use it when looking back and wishing the action had been done differently. Attach ~ㄹ걸 그랬다 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~을걸 그랬다 after another consonant; use the negative form when regretting an action not done.

그 걸 엄마에게 말하지 말걸
I shouldn’t have told my mother that
그 자선 단체에 돈을 안 줄걸
I shouldn’t have given money to that charitable organization

lessons.title: Remaining in a state with 채
lessons.explanation: Original practice for the HTSK Lesson 116 focus. Use the official Unit 5 lesson for the full explanation and additional examples.

cards.translation: The girl came out of the bathroom with the toilet covered by newspaper
cards.explanation: 채 means remaining in a state while another action happens, often translated while still or without changing. Use it when the original state continues during the next action. Use N인 채(로), V-은/는 채(로) or the tense appropriate to the state, then add 로 or the following predicate as shown by HTSK.
